# 08 — Zero-Copy Rules & dbt Schemas via typify

Binding decisions, same status as 05–07. Two decisions:

1. **Zero-copy** as a concrete, checkable rulebook for the Rust code (§1).
2. **dbt file shapes come from dbt-labs/dbt-jsonschema**, with the Rust types
   **generated by `typify`** (§2) — replacing the hand-written YAML structs of
   03 §3/§6.2 as the deserialization target.

## 1. Zero-copy rulebook

"Zero-copy" here means: within a parse or request lifetime, bytes are not
duplicated; owning copies exist only at deliberate, named boundaries. The rules:

### 1.1 Tokens carry spans, not strings

The unified token model (05 §4) stores **no literal text**:

```rust
pub struct Token { pub kind: TokenKind, pub span: Range<u32>, pub line: u32, pub column: u32 }

pub struct ParsedDocument {
    pub text: Arc<str>,                 // the one owner of the document bytes
    pub tokens: TokenIndex,             // spans into `text`
    pub def_tokens: HashMap<Box<str>, Token>,  // CTE names (small, owned keys)
}
impl ParsedDocument { fn literal(&self, t: &Token) -> &str { &self.text[t.span...] } }
```

- Spans are indices, not references — the idiomatic Rust zero-copy pattern that
  avoids self-referential structs. Lifetime safety is trivial because `text`
  and the spans live in the same struct.
- This removes the per-token `String` allocation from the hottest path (full
  retokenize per keystroke, 05 §6.1) — on a typical model file that is
  hundreds of allocations per keystroke gone.
- Everything that consumed `Token.literal` (cursor lookup length math 02 §3.5,
  lookback matches 02 §3.6, map lookups in the features 03 §9) works on
  `&str` slices resolved through `literal()`; map lookups use the borrowed
  slice directly (`HashMap<String, _>::get(&str)` needs no allocation).
- minijinja and sqlparser return owned token values; the merge/convert layer
  (05 §4 step 3) converts them to spans by locating them in the source via the
  positions both libraries report — the owned crate tokens die inside the
  conversion, they are never stored.

### 1.2 Inbound frames borrow

- The reader task (05 §6.2) reuses one growable `Vec<u8>` and hands the
  dispatcher one frame slice at a time.
- Request/notification params deserialize **borrowing from the frame buffer**:
  string fields are `Cow<'a, str>` with `#[serde(borrow)]` (uris, text,
  command names). serde_json borrows when the JSON string has no escapes —
  the common case for uris — and allocates only when it must.
- The **one deliberate copy** on the inbound path: `didOpen`/`didChange`
  document text is copied into the new `Arc<str>` (it must outlive the frame).
  Everything else read from params is used and dropped within the handler.

### 1.3 Scan side slices until the snapshot

- Extraction functions (06 §2, 03 §5–§6) take `&str` and, where a result field
  is a verbatim slice of the source (macro signatures, docs contents, raw
  descriptions), return `&'src str` and defer owning.
- Owning happens exactly once, when results enter the published
  `Arc<DbtContext>` snapshot — snapshots outlive every source buffer, so
  ownership there is the design, not a violation.

### 1.4 Outbound serializes into the frame buffer

The writer task owns a reusable `Vec<u8>`; responses are built as
`write!(buf, "Content-Length: {}\r\n\r\n", n)` + `serde_json::to_writer(&mut buf, &msg)`
(length from a first serialization into the same reused buffer, or
counted via a small counting writer) — no intermediate `String` per response.

### 1.5 Boundaries (allowed owners)

`Arc<str>` document text, `Arc<DbtContext>` snapshots, the graph's `NodeData`,
diagnostics in flight, and typify-generated schema types (§2.4) own their data
by design. The rulebook governs everything *between* those owners. Review
heuristic: a `.to_string()`/`.clone()` inside a parser, extractor, or handler
needs a comment naming which boundary it feeds; otherwise it's a defect.

## 2. dbt schemas: dbt-jsonschema → typify

### 2.1 Source of truth

The reference for every dbt file shape is **dbt-labs/dbt-jsonschema**
(https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-jsonschema). Vendor pinned copies under
`schemas/dbt/`:

| Schema file | Covers |
|---|---|
| `dbt_project.json` | `dbt_project.yml` (03 §3) |
| `dbt_yml_files.json` | properties/schema `.yml` files — models, sources, seeds, snapshots, macros docs (03 §6.2) |
| `packages.json` | `packages.yml` / `package-lock.yml` |
| `selectors.json` | `selectors.yml` |

`schemas/dbt/README` records the upstream commit; updating the schemas is an
explicit, reviewed commit (fetch → regenerate → diff).

### 2.2 Generation with typify (compile-time macro)

Types are generated at compile time with Oxide's `typify::import_types!`
macro, one module per schema:

```rust
pub mod dbt_project {
    typify::import_types!(
        schema = "../../schemas/dbt/processed/dbt_project.json",
        unknown_crates = Allow,
    );
}
```

The macro reads **preprocessed** copies committed under
`schemas/dbt/processed/`, produced from the pristine vendored files by the
committed `schemas/dbt/preprocess.py` (documented typify-0.8 workarounds:
if/then/else stripped, case-duplicate enum values deduped, `+x`/`x` property
collisions resolved, `oneOf [X, null]` collapsed, `default` values dropped).
A CI check regenerates `processed/` and fails on diffs. Trade-off accepted
with this style: the types compile inside the crate build instead of being
reviewable committed Rust — contained by `dbt-ls-schemas` being a
rarely-touched leaf crate (09 §1), so the compile-time story holds.
`typify` is a normal dependency of that crate; generated code additionally
uses `serde` and `regress`.

### 2.3 Replacing the hand-written structs

The generated types replace the hand-written subset structs as the
**deserialization target**:

- 03 §3 `DbtProjectYaml` → `generated::dbt_project::*` (full shape: all paths,
  vars, flags — not just the six fields Go reads).
- 03 §6.2 `PropertiesYaml`/`ModelProperties`/`SourceProperties` →
  `generated::dbt_yml_files::*`.

The 03 algorithms (defaults in §3.3, model/source/variable extraction) read
from the generated types; their *behavior* (which fields are used, the default
rules, output structs) is unchanged. A thin adapter module
(`src/analysis/dbt_schema/mod.rs`) maps generated types → the internal detail
structs so the rest of the code never imports `generated::`.

### 2.4 Positions: the annotated layer stays

typify output is plain serde — **it cannot carry YAML node positions**, and the
features need ranges (definitions jump to names/vars, 03 §4/§6). The pipeline
parses each YAML file **once** with saphyr and produces two things:

1. a `serde` value (saphyr tree → `serde_json::Value` bridge) deserialized into
   the typify types — the shape-accurate data;
2. a **position side-table** from the same saphyr markers, recording ranges for
   exactly the paths features need: model names, source/table names, top-level
   & project-scoped vars, `config.alias` (the 03 §3.1 annotated layer, reduced
   to a side-table instead of wrapping every field).

Lookup key: a path like `models[3].name` → `Position`. The adapter (§2.3)
joins shape data and positions when building `ModelDetails`/`Source`/`Variable`.

Zero-copy note: generated types own their strings; acceptable — YAML parsing is
scan-side (never on the keystroke path) and feeds the owning snapshot boundary
(§1.5).

### 2.5 Env-var resolution unchanged

`{{ env_var(...) }}` preprocessing (03 §3.2, 03 §7.3) still runs on the raw
file string before the saphyr parse, for `dbt_project.yml` only.

### 2.6 Unlocked later (specced separately when picked up)

- **YAML validation diagnostics**: validate dbt files against the vendored
  schemas (via typify's serde errors, or `jsonschema` crate for full
  keyword coverage) and publish problems with positions from the side-table.
- **Field-name completion in `.yml` files**: offer property names/enums from
  the schema at the cursor's YAML path.

### 2.7 Testing

- Snapshot (insta) the adapter output over `testdata/` — must equal the
  hand-written-struct results the 03 tests already pin (same
  `ModelDetails`/`Source`/`Variable` vectors).
- One rstest case per schema file proving the vendored schema parses and the
  generated types deserialize a real-world sample (jaffle_shop files).
- Regeneration CI check per §2.2.

## 3. Layout & manifest deltas (amends 05 §1/§8)

```
schemas/dbt/                         # vendored dbt-jsonschema files + README (pin)
src/analysis/dbt_schema/
├── mod.rs                           # adapter: generated types + position side-table → detail structs
├── positions.rs                     # saphyr walk → side-table (replaces blanket AnnotatedField)
└── generated/                       # committed cargo-typify output (do not edit)
```

Manifest: no new runtime deps (generated code uses `serde` only); `cargo-typify`
documented as a required dev tool next to Zig (07 §5) in the README.

## 4. Feature-batch schema deltas (binding)

- `prune_for_server` widens to keep `exposures`, `metrics`,
  `semantic_models`, `saved_queries` and `groups` (the generated types
  already exist); `packages` gets its first consumer (packages.yml).
- dbt ARTIFACTS (SUPERSEDED): the artifact schemas ARE now vendored —
  pristine copies of schemas.getdbt.com dbt/{run-results/v6, sources/v3,
  catalog/v1, manifest/v12}.json under `schemas/dbt/artifacts/`
  (upstream commit pinned in `schemas/dbt/README`). The official
  schemas are strict (`additionalProperties: false`, long `required`
  lists, versioned status enums) in ways dbt itself never honors across
  versions, so `preprocess.py --mode=artifact` manufactures the 03 §10
  leniency before typify: strip the strictness and every `required`
  (adapters re-impose unique_id by dropping the ROW, not the file),
  collapse all-string-enum unions to plain strings, merge all-object
  unions into one open shape (sources' RuntimeError|Output rows),
  relax string-valued open maps (env) to any-valued, keep [X, null]
  branches (typify renders Option; dbt writes literal nulls), and drop
  format/propertyNames/const pins. The manifest compiles a documented
  PROJECTION only (`--mode=manifest-projection`): typifying the 946 KB
  schema would cost thousands of types for two lookups; the projected
  field names are asserted against the pristine text so an upstream
  rename fails `just gen-schemas`, never runtime.
  `cogitator_schemas::artifacts` is the sanctioned re-export of these
  generated modules — artifacts carry no YAML positions, so the
  side-table discipline behind the "nothing imports `generated::`"
  invariant does not apply; cogitator-analysis maps them into its lean
  public indexes immediately.
- Cached scan payloads (`PropertiesFile` and nested entries, RawMacro,
  RawDocsBlock, graph NodeKind/EdgeKind) gain serde derives so the scan
  cache can persist; wire zero-copy rules (§1) are unaffected — the
  persistence path serializes owned snapshot data off the hot path.
